sampleRecords.Name: report omni 1
sampleRecords.Notes:
Here is a summary of the wearing experience for each clothing item, based on the wearing reports:

\*\*apricot french rm30\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. Works well with a big/hugo bra though breast size can look a bit small; the not-diao-dai design keeps the shoulder comfortable without irritation. Middle-thick fabric feels hotter and sweaty at noon, but at night it's fine under a fan; long dress keeps legs warm though it can get cold around 4am.

\*\*blue diao dai thick\*\* — Rated \*Middle beautiful\*. Breast looks full and beautiful but the dress cut makes it dip a little in the middle; the shoulder drops and needs an outer fit, making it quite hot. Thick fabric is hot and sweaty, though still okay sleeping under a fan; feels like a dress rather than pants (easy to fold up).

\*\*blue dress\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. Full and beautiful shape, best with a big bra (small bra needs manual adjustment). Thin chiffon fabric only gets hot at the fitted chest area, other areas stay cool; short dress means cold legs at night. Not-diao-dai design keeps shoulders comfortable.

\*\*Blue french dress\*\* — Rated \*Middle beautiful\*. Mid breast looks beautiful from the top and feels heavier due to the center-breast bra pairing; the not-diao-dai style avoids shoulder irritation. Feels like a dress not pants.

\*\*Blue side flower dress\*\* — Rated \*Middle beautiful\*. Full and beautiful shape, but the diao dai design irritates and hurts the shoulder. Middle-thick lace fabric makes it hotter and sweaty, though only lightly sweaty in mild weather; middle-thick skirt keeps legs from getting too cold.

\*\*Green diao dai\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. A tight mid design makes the bra sit smaller and stick to the chest; the diao dai irritates the shoulder but is not hot at noon. Middle-thick lace fabric is warmer and sweaty; short dress with middle-thick material is only slightly cold on legs.

\*\*hugo bra\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. Worn for long durations as a bra item.

\*\*pink bridesmaid\*\* — Rated \*Middle beautiful\*. The mid design isn't very flattering with either small or big bra; shoulder sometimes drops. Thick fabric is hot and sweaty; the long, thin skirt inner tends to stick to the legs and may cause sweat.

\*\*pink diao dai chiffon\*\* — Rated \*Middle beautiful\*. Tight mid design squeezes the bra smaller and sticks to the chest, looking less flattering and hot at the middle; other areas and the thin chiffon skirt stay cool. Diao dai irritates the shoulder; short dress means cold legs at night.

\*\*pink flower rm30\*\* — Rated \*Not so beautiful\*. Big bra gives a better shape but the waist design is ugly with a lot of wrinkling (zhouwhen); not-diao-dai keeps shoulders comfortable. Middle-thick lace is hot and sweaty; short skirt makes legs moderately cold.

\*\*pink lace old\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. Mid breast looks a little small with a small bra but is still feminine and okay; not-diao-dai avoids shoulder irritation. Middle-thick lace is hot and sweaty but okay sleeping under a fan.

\*\*pink side flower dress\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. Mid breast is a little small with the hugo bra but still feminine; the not-diao-dai design keeps the shoulder comfortable.

\*\*pink white dress\*\* — Rated \*Not so beautiful\*. The tight mid design makes the bra smaller and wrinkled (zhouwhen), sticking to the chest; the wide diao dai makes the shoulder drop and irritates but doesn't hurt or feel hot at noon. Middle-thick plain fabric is hot, sweaty and tight to the chest; short middle-thick skirt makes legs moderately cold.

\*\*red soft big new\*\* — Rated \*Not so beautiful\*. Full and beautiful shape but needs a big bra and a waist belt, and gets hot and sweaty at noon; not-diao-dai is comfortable on the shoulder though the long shoulder size may feel hot. Long dress is hot at noon but keeps legs warm at night.

\*\*white heavy new\*\* — Rated \*Middle beautiful\*. Full and warm breast with a big bra; with hugo bra breast looks quite small. Comfortable at night under a fan; long dress generally keeps legs warm, though on some nights the skirt rides out and legs feel cold.

\*\*white marry old\*\* — Rated \*Beautiful\*. Full and warm breast with hugo/big bra and nicely centered; blue big bra makes it look very large. Not-diao-dai keeps the shoulder comfortable. Thick fabric is hot and sweaty but okay under a fan; long dress keeps legs warm, though the short skirt inner sometimes rides up at night.

\*\*Note:\*\* A few reports had little or no written feedback and only recorded wear time, so they aren't detailed above.

Would you like this broken down further — for example, comparing which items stay coolest at noon or which pair best with each bra?

sampleRecords.Name: Wardrobe analysis
sampleRecords.Notes:
# Wardrobe Overview

## Scope and data limitations

### Observed facts
- The requested scope is **34 clothes**, but the supplied source contains **32 complete records and one partially visible record**, **“Green diao dai.”** The source is truncated before that item ends, and the 34th record is not visible.
- The visible records comprise:
  - **23 complete dresses**
  - **7 bras**
  - **2 T-shirts**
  - **1 partially supplied dress**
- The actual linked wearing reports were not included as raw records. Only item-level summaries mention their dates, counts, duplicates, and selected findings.
- This report incorporates all report-derived information visible in those summaries, but it cannot independently review every linked report or verify omitted details.

### Inference
The wardrobe is overwhelmingly dress-focused. The most important recurring issues are heat, loose or unattractive chest construction, incomplete wash tracking, and inconsistent data entry.

---

# 1. Usage and wardrobe value

## Observed facts

The meaning and time period of **“wearing frequency” are undefined**, so these numbers cannot safely be treated as confirmed wear counts. Nevertheless, the highest recorded values among the complete records are:

- **white marry old — 160**
- **white baby dress — 150**
- **pink lady dress — 140**
- **pink lace old — 106**
- **green dress — 100**
- **Blue french dress — 45**
- **blue dress — 39**
- **white marry 2 — 37**
- **pink side flower dress — 30**

   Wash **hugo bra new 2 (37:00)**, **Blue french dress (19:00)**, **purple old bra (17:30)**, **pink diao dai chiffon (12:00)**, **pink side flower dress (10:00)**, **white marry old (10:00)**, and **Blue side flower dress (8:00)** before further wear.

2. **Fully dry every wet item before storage.**  
   Prioritize **white wedding big, yellow diao dai, red soft big new, pink bridesmaid**, and **Blue french dress**. Give extra airflow and drying time to the thick middle or thick-chiffon areas.

3. **Use a climate-based rotation.**  
   Make **blue dress** the primary documented hot-weather option. Use thin chiffon dresses in mild or warm conditions. Reserve the thick “white marry” dresses, lace dresses, **white baby dress**, **green dress**, and **Blue french dress** for cooler, evening, or air-conditioned use.

   Test **green dress** and **blue diao dai thick** with a supportive bra and secured tie. Test **white light new** after tightening the tie. Record standing, sitting, and side fit separately rather than putting standing comments in the sitting field.

   - **yellow diao dai:** release if one cool indoor trial does not improve the loose fit or appearance.

   If shoulder irritation and bra-related heat recur, remove it from regular rotation; repeated physical irritation outweighs its attractive upper-bust view.

7. **Inspect the old and fragile bras.**  
   Check the elastic, cups, seams, side coverage, and straps of **purple old bra, pink old bra, blue old bra**, and especially **small bra**. Retire any bra with weakened elastic, tears, or insecure side coverage. Wash **small bra** gently because its material is reported to break easily.

   Its Not-hot rating is promising, but record total duration, sweat, body sticking, strap comfort, center and side coverage, and seated fit before relying on it.

9. **Correct the database before calculating value or disposal priority.**
